criteria.text: The participant has advanced unresectable or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer that has progressed following treatment with a CDK4/6 inhibitor in the adjuvant or advanced/metastatic setting.

The participant has advanced or metastatic platinum-resistant or platinum-refractory high grade serous epithelial ovarian cancer, fallopian tube cancer, or primary peritoneal cancer, with known amplification of CCNE-1 that progressed after standard systemic therapy.
The participant has advanced or metastatic solid tumor with known amplification of CCNE-1 that has progressed after standard therapy, been intolerant to or is ineligible for standard therapy.
The participant has at least one measurable lesion as defined by RECIST v1.1 that has not previously been irradiated.
The participant has an ECOG performance status score of 0 or 1.

The participant has adequate organ function as demonstrated by the following laboratory values: Hemoglobin ≥ 9.0 g/dL, Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) ≥ 1.5 × 10^9/L, Platelet count ≥ 100 × 10^9/L, Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of ≥60 mL/min, Total bilirubin ≤ 1.5 × ULN (Part A and B); AST and ALT ≤ 2.5 × ULN (≤ 5 × ULN in the presence of liver metastases) (Part A and B); Patients with Gilbert's syndrome with a total bilirubin ≤ 2.0 × ULN and direct bilirubin within normal limits (Part C).
The participant has a negative pregnancy test.
The participant has received previous therapy with a CDK2/4/6 inhibitor or CDK2 inhibitor.

The participant has central nervous system (CNS) metastases or spinal cord compression that is associated with progressive neurological symptoms or requires corticosteroids (within 4 weeks of enrollment) to control the CNS disease.
The participant has known intracranial hemorrhage and/or bleeding diatheses.
The participant has visceral crisis, lymphangitic spread, or leptomeningeal carcinomatosis.

The participant has clinically active ongoing interstitial lung disease (ILD) of any etiology, including drug-induced ILD, and radiation pneumonitis within 28 days prior to initiation of study treatment.
The participant has a resting QTcF > 470 msec, a history of prolonged QT syndrome or Torsades de pointes, or a familial history of prolonged QT syndrome.
The participant has uncontrolled cardiovascular disease (including hypertension) with or without medication.

The participant has a history of other malignancies, except for adequately treated basal or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin; curatively treated in situ carcinoma of the uterine cervix, prostate cancer, or superficial bladder cancer; or other curatively treated solid tumor with no evidence of disease for ≥ 3 years.

The participant has known HIV infection, including AIDS-related illness, or has active, uncontrolled infection (viral, bacterial, or fungal), including tuberculosis, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, or COVID-19 infection (symptoms and a positive test result).
The participant requires treatment with a prohibited medication or herbal remedy that cannot be discontinued at least 2 weeks before the start of study drug administration.

The participant has a planned or anticipated need for a major surgical procedure within 28 days of the first dose of study drug (procedures such as central venous catheter placement, tumor needle biopsy, and feeding tube placement are not considered major surgical procedures).
The participant is unwilling or unable to comply with scheduled visits, study drug administration plan, laboratory tests, or other study procedures and study restrictions.
The participant has received radical radiotherapy within 28 days prior to study entry or palliative radiotherapy within 2 weeks prior to study entry.
The participant has received systemic anti-cancer therapy within 21 days or at least 5 half-lives, whichever is less, prior to the first dose of the study drug.
The participant has prior irradiation to > 25% of the bone marrow.
The participant has had previous high-dose chemotherapy requiring prior stem cell transplant.
The participant has participated in other studies involving investigational drug(s) within 4 weeks prior to study entry.
The participant has known or suspected hypersensitivity to active ingredient/excipients in INX-315 or fulvestrant or abemaciclib.

The participant has known difficulty in swallowing or tolerating oral medications, or conditions which would impair absorption of oral medications such as active inflammatory gastrointestinal disease, uncontrolled nausea or vomiting (i.e., CTCAE ≥ Grade 3 despite antiemetic therapy), ongoing gastrointestinal obstruction/motility disorder/active inflammation, malabsorption syndrome, chronic diarrhea, known diverticular disease or previous gastric resection or lap band surgery.

The participant has a serious and/or uncontrolled pre-existing medical condition(s) that, in the judgment of the Investigator or the Sponsor, would preclude participation in this study (for example but not limited to, interstitial lung disease, severe dyspnea at rest or requiring oxygen therapy, history of major surgical resection involving the stomach or small bowel, or preexisting Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis or a preexisting chronic condition resulting in baseline Grade 2 or higher diarrhea).

transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any issues tolerating oral medications, uncontrolled nausea or vomiting, ongoing GI obstruction or motility issues, chronic diarrhea, known diverticular disease, or have you had previous gastric resection or lap band surgery?

transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any serious or uncontrolled medical conditions, such as interstitial lung disease, severe shortness of breath, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or chronic diarrhea?

transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, is your Crohn's disease currently well-controlled with no active symptoms or flare-ups?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, my Crohn's is well-controlled on Humira. I don't have active flare-ups.
